stories.body: Donald Trump said no talks with Iran were planned and maintained that the Strait of Hormuz remained open, despite reduced shipping traffic and reports of a projectile striking a vessel. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Washington was seeking negotiations after failing to force Iran to surrender. Oman and Iran were reported to be nearing an agreement concerning the waterway, while the United Arab Emirates said two Iranian ballistic missiles had landed in or near its waters.
stories.headline: Iran and the US trade claims over stalled talks as tensions rise around the Strait of Hormuz

stories.body: South Korea said its annual Ulchi Freedom Shield exercise with the United States would end on 21 August, six days earlier than planned, after a request from Washington. Associated field training will also be reduced, with some events cancelled or converted to simulations. Trump had called the drills costly and hostile to North Korea, citing his relationship with Kim Jong Un and linking his decision to Seoul's refusal to assist the US and Israel in the war on Iran. South Korean Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said officials in both governments had not known about the directive beforehand.
stories.headline: US and South Korea sharply shorten joint military drills after Trump order

stories.body: The United States called Israeli airstrikes on Syria's Abu al-Duhur airbase an unnecessary escalation that would not advance regional stability. Syrian media said eight strikes hit the runway and storage facilities at the base in Idlib province. Israel said Syria had been close to breaching a security status quo by permitting Turkish troops to deploy there, but Turkey rejected the allegation as frivolous and said it was intended to justify unlawful attacks on Syrian sovereignty. Syria described the strikes as unjustified aggression.
stories.headline: US condemns Israeli strikes on a Syrian airbase as Turkey rejects Israeli allegations

stories.body: Opening arguments began in a landmark trial in Oakland, California, in which four states accuse Meta of deliberately designing Facebook and Instagram to addict children and concealing harms to young users. The case is part of a 2023 lawsuit brought by 29 states alleging violations of child privacy and consumer-protection laws. Prosecutors cited internal Meta research on teen wellbeing and argued that the company prioritized engagement and data collection over safety. Meta disputed that social-media addiction exists or that research establishes a clear causal link with poor adolescent wellbeing, and pointed to protections including teen accounts and parental controls.
stories.headline: Meta faces landmark US trial over claims Facebook and Instagram harmed children

stories.body: Republican Byron Donalds and Democrat David Jolly won their respective Florida gubernatorial primaries and will face each other in November to succeed term-limited Governor Ron DeSantis. Donalds, a congressman endorsed by Trump, prevailed in the Republican contest. Jolly, a former Republican congressman and Trump critic, won the Democratic nomination. The Florida primary also produced notable congressional and Senate results, including progressive state representative Angie Nixon's upset win in the Democratic Senate primary and the defeat of Republican Representative Cory Mills in his House primary.
stories.headline: Byron Donalds and David Jolly win Florida primaries for governor

stories.body: Trump-endorsed candidates lost several Republican primaries, including Wyoming Superintendent of Public Instruction Megan Degenfelder, who was defeated in the state's gubernatorial contest by state Senator Eric Barlow. In Florida, Representative Cory Mills lost his House primary to former television anchor Ryan Elijah, while former Trump administration official Catalina Lauf lost a congressional primary to media executive Jim Schwartzel. The defeats follow other recent losses by Trump-backed candidates and suggest that the president's endorsement has been less decisive in several 2026 primary races, particularly for governor.
stories.headline: Trump-backed candidates suffer primary defeats in Florida and Wyoming

stories.body: Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro is introducing policy changes to sharply limit data-center development and expand the review process for proposed projects. The move comes amid growing bipartisan concern among political leaders about the rapid growth of data centers and their effects on electricity demand, water use and local communities.
stories.headline: Pennsylvania moves to sharply limit data-center development and expand reviews

stories.body: The European Commission said migrants remaining illegally in Ceuta should be returned to Morocco quickly, including unaccompanied children, arguing that EU return rules provide for such cases. The statement came as the number of registered minors in Ceuta rose to 2,168 after a large late-July crossing. Spain's Youth and Children Ministry rejected the approach described by Brussels, saying the best interests and protection of each child must take precedence and that children cannot be treated as commodities.
stories.headline: European Commission backs returns of unaccompanied migrant children in Ceuta to Morocco

stories.body: Spain's government is pursuing two tracks in its response to Ceuta's migration crisis: accelerating the removal of migrants without grounds for asylum or regularisation while providing accommodation for minors and asylum applicants whose cases are processed. The government says it does not plan to transfer migrants to mainland Spain, despite pressure on local services and delays in opening promised accommodation. More than 2,000 minors have been identified since 30 July, with Ceuta's capacity severely overstretched; local volunteers have warned that vulnerable children remain in inadequate conditions.
stories.headline: Spain's government seeks to balance care for migrant minors with faster removals in Ceuta

stories.body: A shallow magnitude-4.8 earthquake struck near Gójar in Granada province, leaving three people with minor injuries, damaging buildings and prompting the evacuation of about 600 residents in Las Gabias. Emergency services received more than 500 calls reporting cracks and falling debris. It was the latest in a sequence that has produced more than 450 aftershocks since another 4.8-magnitude quake on 15 August. Seismologists say the activity may be an earthquake swarm, a recurrent phenomenon in this seismically active area where the African and Eurasian plates meet.
stories.headline: New 4.8-magnitude earthquake hits Granada, causing injuries and damage

stories.body: A fast-moving wildfire in the Las Hurdes area of Cáceres forced the evacuation of roughly 700 people from ten small settlements and 38 residents of a care home for people with disabilities. Extremadura raised its wildfire response to level 2 after the blaze, which began near Robledo in Pinofranqueado, was described as highly virulent and beyond extinguishing capacity for much of the day. More than 150 personnel and 17 aircraft were deployed, with additional crews, aircraft and military emergency units expected to reinforce the operation.
stories.headline: Wildfire in Las Hurdes forces evacuations of more than 700 people

stories.body: Barcelona has increased the budget for grants to homeowners' associations that prohibit tourist flats in their buildings from €56,000 to €256,000 after receiving more than 80 applications, exceeding expectations. The city extended the application deadline to 31 December. Associations can receive up to half of the administrative costs of changing or creating their statutes to restrict tourist use, up to €1,500 for amendments to existing rules and €2,500 for new statutes. The measure supports the city's wider plan not to renew licences for more than 10,000 tourist apartments after 2028.
stories.headline: Barcelona expands grants for apartment blocks that ban tourist flats

stories.body: An indefinite strike by Groundforce ground-handling staff at Barcelona-El Prat has left about 6,000 bags failing to reach their destinations and affected around 270 flights after two weeks, according to the strike committee. Workers began the stoppage on 4 August and say the company has refused to negotiate over health and safety, staffing levels, shift patterns, rest periods and work-life balance. Groundforce serves about 20 airlines at both terminals, with Lufthansa, Air Europa and ITA Airways routes among those most affected.
stories.headline: Groundforce strike at Barcelona-El Prat leaves thousands of bags and hundreds of flights affected

stories.body: Barcelona is expected to experience another day of intense heat and humidity, with temperatures of 32C to 34C in the city and highs approaching 37C to 39C in parts of the metropolitan area. Heat warnings remain in force, including for very warm nighttime temperatures. Weather is expected to turn more unstable from Thursday evening into Friday, bringing a risk of locally heavy showers and thunderstorms around the coast and pre-coastal areas, followed by a noticeable easing of temperatures.
stories.headline: Barcelona faces intense heat before storms and cooler weather later this week

stories.body: Collserola park officials have called for wider vegetation-cleared protection strips around homes after a 14 August fire on Sant Pere Màrtir burned at least 10 hectares and led to confinement orders for nearby residents. The existing 25-metre strips were designed in 1994 chiefly to prevent fires spreading from urban areas into woodland, but officials say the greater risk now is intense forest fires reaching homes. The park also wants upgraded helicopter bases and water-loading systems, while Civil Protection stressed that residents need timely information and knowledge of self-protection measures during wildfire emergencies.
stories.headline: Collserola calls for wider wildfire protection strips around homes after recent fire
